title: Smart backpressure protocols for client SDK and runtime
creator: Ava Nguyen
description: Goal: define and ship a consistent backpressure and retry surface across client SDKs and the serving runtime that protects SLOs during overload and multi-region failover, while enabling safe hedged requests and explicit idempotency for stateful operations. The work covers: 1) a client-side backpressure protocol (soft and hard limits, token-bucket shaped retry windows), 2) an interoperable idempotency token contract (header name, TTL, dedupe semantics), 3) hedged request heuristics (when to allow hedging vs. standard retry), 4) runtime admission control and circuit breaker mappings, and 5) telemetry and rollout plan. This ticket produces the SDK surface changes, runtime admission API, compatibility tests, and a migration playbook.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SDKs expose a small, language-native BackpressurePolicy with clear defaults that do not change existing behavior for current customers. 2) Contract for idempotency key header (X-Idempotency-Key) documented with TTL semantics and server-side dedup window. 3) Hedged request mode enabled only when operation is marked idempotent or stateless; SDK default: off for mutating endpoints. 4) Runtime implements token-bucket admission with fast-path shed and circuit-breaker hooks that map to SDK signals. 5) End-to-end integration tests covering multi-region failover, spike load shedding, and hedged-request correctness. 6) Telemetry: per-route backpressure events, hedged vs primary latency histograms, idempotency dedupe counts. 7) Rollout can be toggled per-customer via console flags and has an automatic fallback to previous behavior on increased error-rate.
implementation_notes: - Client SDK changes: add BackpressurePolicy object with fields: maxInFlight, burstAllowance, baseBackoffMs, maxBackoffMs, allowHedging boolean, idempotencyHeader default 'X-Idempotency-Key'. Provide simple builder and sane defaults tuned for low-latency interactive traffic. - Server/runtime: admission controller exposes runtime API: /v1/internal/admit?route=<route> that accepts tokens and returns admit/reject/slowdown plus suggested client backoff metadata. Implement token-bucket per-route with weights derived from SLOs and capacity hints. - Hedging: implement conservative hedging window: issue second request after p95+20% of historic latency if allowHedging is true and request is idempotent. Hedge only once; cancel slower inflight. - Idempotency TTL: default 60s for most generation calls, configurable per-route. Dedup key hashing must include route signature and model version. - Circuit breakers: map runtime circuit state to SDK so SDK can start exponential backoff on circuit-open with jitter. - Telemetry: emit events to metrics pipeline: backpressure_admit{route,decision}, hedged_request{route,result,latency_primary,latency_hedge}, idempotency_dedupe{route,hit/miss}. - Compatibility: SDKs should not require server upgrade; runtime will honor unknown idempotency headers by treating as opaque tokens. - Migration: staged rollout to canary customers with console flip and traffic shaping rules.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: improper idempotency handling could lead to silent drops or duplicate stateful operations. Mitigation: require explicit opt-in for mutating endpoints; default hedging off for endpoints marked mutable. Risk: new backpressure signals may increase client-side latency for some low-volume customers. Mitigation: provide conservative defaults and per-customer overrides via console. Risk: incorrect dedupe TTL may mask retried legitimate retries. Mitigation: log dedupe events and provide quick dashboard to inspect dedupe rate per route before increasing dedupe windows.
test_plan: - Unit tests for SDK BackpressurePolicy behaviors (token consumption, backoff growth, hedging decision). - Integration: synthetic traffic generator that creates p99 spikes and verifies runtime admission behavior and client heed of slowdowns. - Multi-region failover test: induce region N+1 outage and verify hedging/failover reduces tail latency and does not cause double-applies for idempotent-marked calls. - Chaos test: flip circuit-breaker to open and measure SDK backoff responses and automatic fallback after cooldown. - Canaries: gradual rollout to 5% of customers for 72h with automatic rollback on error-rate > 2x baseline.
migration_playbook: 1) Merge SDK changes behind feature flags; release patch to each supported language. 2) Enable runtime admission endpoints in staging; run compatibility tests. 3) Configure a small set of non-critical routes in canary to accept idempotency headers and backpressure hints. 4) Monitor dedupe metrics and hedging latencies; iterate thresholds. 5) Open console toggle to enable for customer-facing routes and monitor for 7 days. 6) Gradually expand to all routes, then flip default flags. 7) Communicate breaking behavior and recommended SDK upgrades in release notes and customer briefings.
